title: Humans on Duty: Keeping AI Safe
subject: AI-Literacy
chapter: 10. Humans on Duty: Keeping AI Safe
description: Practice on AI accountability and safety for grade 4 learners: who is responsible when AI makes mistakes, how tasks split between humans and AI, what laws require of AI companies, and real scenarios (an AI Reading Buddy, an AI doctor app, a broken homework helper, a food delivery app, a gaming app charge, and the real DoNotPay 'robot lawyer' FTC case) that show why humans must stay on duty to keep AI safe.

questions.topic: What Is Accountability in AI
questions.question: What does "accountability" mean in the world of AI?
options: AI taking care of itself
Being responsible and answerable for AI's actions
Making AI faster and smarter
Giving AI more colours and shapes
questions.explanation: The worksheet defines accountability as being responsible and answerable for AI's actions — not AI looking after itself or being made faster.

questions.topic: What Is Accountability in AI
questions.question: Which of these best describes 'accountability' in the world of AI?
options: An AI system fixing its own mistakes without any help
Someone being responsible and having to answer for what an AI system does
A company adding more features to its AI
A machine learning to think exactly like a human
questions.explanation: Accountability means a person or company is responsible and must answer for what an AI system does.

questions.topic: What Is Accountability in AI
questions.question: Accountability in AI means that the AI takes care of itself, with no humans involved.
questions.explanation: Accountability means a human or company is responsible and answerable — it does not mean the AI looks after itself.

questions.topic: What Is Accountability in AI
questions.question: The worksheet is titled 'Who holds legal responsibility in the world of AI?' This question is really asking us about...
options: Which colours AI prefers
Who is accountable when something goes wrong with AI
How fast AI can work
How many people use an AI app
questions.explanation: "Legal responsibility" is another way of asking who is accountable when AI causes a problem.

questions.topic: What Is Accountability in AI
questions.question: Why is 'being responsible and answerable' a better description of accountability than 'making AI faster and smarter'?
options: Because accountability is about who must answer for AI's actions, not about improving AI's performance
Because AI must always be made faster
Because accountability and speed mean the same thing
Because only computers can be accountable
questions.explanation: Accountability is about responsibility for actions, which is a completely different idea from making AI faster or smarter.

questions.topic: What Is Accountability in AI
questions.question: A student says, 'Accountability means the AI computer itself must promise never to make a mistake.' What is wrong with this idea?
options: Accountability is about people/companies being responsible and answerable, not the AI computer making promises
Nothing is wrong, this is correct
AI computers cannot make mistakes so this doesn't matter
Accountability only applies to humans who play video games
questions.explanation: Accountability belongs to the humans and companies responsible for AI, not to a promise made by the machine itself.

questions.topic: What Is Accountability in AI
questions.question: 'Making AI faster and smarter' is the same thing as accountability.
questions.explanation: Making AI faster and smarter is about performance, not about being responsible and answerable for AI's actions.

questions.topic: What Is Accountability in AI
questions.question: Select ALL statements that correctly describe accountability in AI.
options: It means being responsible for AI's actions
It means being answerable when AI causes a problem
It means AI takes care of itself
It means only making AI colourful
questions.explanation: Accountability is about being responsible and answerable — not about AI taking care of itself or being made colourful.

questions.topic: What Is Accountability in AI
questions.question: The title of this chapter is 'Humans on Duty: Keeping AI Safe.' What does 'on duty' suggest about humans and AI?
options: Humans must stay responsible and watch over AI
Humans have no role once AI is built
AI replaces humans completely
Humans only build AI once and never check it again
questions.explanation: "On duty" suggests humans must keep actively watching over and taking responsibility for AI, not walk away once it is built.

questions.topic: What Is Accountability in AI
questions.question: Which situation best shows 'accountability' in action?
options: A company fixes its AI app and tells users when something goes wrong
A company blames the computer and does nothing
A company hides mistakes made by its AI
A company ignores complaints about its AI
questions.explanation: Fixing a problem and being honest with users is exactly what being responsible and answerable looks like.

questions.topic: What Is Accountability in AI
questions.question: Accountability means someone must be ready to ____ for what AI does.
options: answer
hide
ignore
delete
questions.explanation: Accountability literally means being ready to answer for AI's actions.

questions.topic: What Is Accountability in AI
questions.question: Which word is closest in meaning to 'accountable'?
options: responsible
invisible
automatic
colourful
questions.explanation: 'Accountable' is closest in meaning to 'responsible' — both mean being answerable for actions.

questions.topic: What Is Accountability in AI
questions.question: Being accountable for AI means being ready to explain and take responsibility if the AI causes a problem.
questions.explanation: This is exactly what accountability means — being responsible and answerable.

questions.topic: What Is Accountability in AI
questions.question: If an AI app makes a mistake and no person or company takes responsibility, what is missing?
options: Accountability
Electricity
Internet connection
A new app icon
questions.explanation: When no one takes responsibility for an AI mistake, accountability is missing.

questions.topic: What Is Accountability in AI
questions.question: Which of these is the BEST reason accountability matters for AI?
options: Without accountability, no one would have to fix AI mistakes or protect users
AI never makes mistakes, so accountability is not needed
Accountability only matters for adults, not students
Accountability slows down how AI is built
questions.explanation: Accountability makes sure someone must fix mistakes and protect users — without it, AI mistakes could go uncorrected.

questions.topic: What Is Accountability in AI
questions.question: The opposite of being accountable is...
options: refusing to take responsibility
testing carefully
fixing mistakes quickly
explaining problems honestly
questions.explanation: Refusing to take responsibility is the opposite of being accountable.

questions.topic: What Is Accountability in AI
questions.question: Select ALL statements that are TRUE about accountability in AI.
options: It means someone must answer for AI's actions
It disappears once an AI app is sold to users
It is part of what this chapter calls being 'on duty'
It only applies to people, never to companies
questions.explanation: Accountability means answering for AI's actions and staying 'on duty' — it does not disappear after selling an app, and it applies to companies too.

questions.topic: What Is Accountability in AI
questions.question: Who can be held accountable when an AI app causes a problem?
options: The company or people responsible for the AI
Nobody, since AI works on its own
Only the student using the app
The electricity company
questions.explanation: The company or people responsible for building and running the AI are the ones held accountable.

questions.topic: What Is Accountability in AI
questions.question: According to the chapter, accountability disappears once an AI has been sold to the public.
questions.explanation: The chapter's examples (the AI doctor app and the robot lawyer) show that companies remain accountable even after their AI product is being used by the public.

questions.topic: What Is Accountability in AI
questions.question: Which best sums up what this whole chapter is teaching about accountability?
options: Even though AI can act on its own, humans and companies remain responsible for keeping it safe and fixing its mistakes
AI should be left alone once it is built
Accountability is only about making AI look impressive
Accountability means blaming the user for AI mistakes
questions.explanation: This is the chapter's central message — humans stay on duty and responsible even though AI can act automatically.

questions.topic: What Is Accountability in AI
questions.question: Which is NOT what accountability means in AI, according to the worksheet's quick knowledge check?
options: Being responsible for AI's actions
Being answerable when AI causes a problem
Making AI faster and smarter
Someone having to explain what went wrong
questions.explanation: "Making AI faster and smarter" is about improving performance, not about being responsible and answerable — that is what accountability means.

questions.topic: What Is Accountability in AI
questions.question: Select ALL examples that show a company being accountable for its AI.
options: Explaining what went wrong
Fixing the problem
Pretending nothing happened
Testing the AI before selling it
questions.explanation: Explaining problems, fixing them, and testing beforehand all show accountability. Pretending nothing happened is the opposite of accountability.

questions.topic: Humans vs AI: Who Does What
questions.question: In the 'Reading Buddy' example, what does the AI Reading Buddy do?
options: Suggests books for learners
Grades homework
Teaches maths
Cleans the classroom
questions.explanation: The worksheet describes an AI Reading Buddy that suggests books for learners.

questions.topic: Humans vs AI: Who Does What
questions.question: The AI Reading Buddy in the example always gives perfect suggestions and never makes mistakes.
questions.explanation: The worksheet says the Reading Buddy 'sometimes gives strange suggestions,' so it does not always work perfectly.

questions.topic: Humans vs AI: Who Does What
questions.question: Who should fix the Reading Buddy when it suggests the wrong book?
options: Humans
The AI on its own
No one
The book itself
questions.explanation: Fixing the Reading Buddy's mistakes is a 'Humans do' task in the worksheet's sorting activity.

questions.topic: Humans vs AI: Who Does What
questions.question: Who should choose the rules that the Reading Buddy must follow?
options: Humans
The AI on its own
The books
No one
questions.explanation: Choosing which rules the Reading Buddy must follow is a 'Humans do' task.

questions.topic: Humans vs AI: Who Does What
questions.question: Which task is something the AI actually performs by itself?
options: Noticing reading patterns in learners' choices
Fixing the Reading Buddy's mistakes
Choosing the rules the Reading Buddy follows
Making sure the Reading Buddy is safe
questions.explanation: 'Noticing reading patterns in learners' choices' is an 'AI performs' task — quickly spotting patterns in data is what AI does.

questions.topic: Humans vs AI: Who Does What
questions.question: Which task is something the AI actually performs?
options: Suggesting books quickly
Deciding the safety rules
Fixing bugs in the code
Being legally responsible
questions.explanation: 'Suggesting books quickly' is an 'AI performs' task — giving fast suggestions is the AI's everyday job.

questions.topic: Humans vs AI: Who Does What
questions.question: Select ALL the tasks that are 'Humans do' tasks for the Reading Buddy.
options: Fixing the Reading Buddy when it suggests the wrong book
Choosing which rules the Reading Buddy must follow
Noticing reading patterns in learners' choices
Making sure the Reading Buddy is safe to use
questions.explanation: Fixing mistakes, choosing rules, and ensuring safety are all 'Humans do' tasks. Noticing patterns is an 'AI performs' task.

questions.topic: Humans vs AI: Who Does What
questions.question: Select ALL the tasks that are 'AI performs' tasks for the Reading Buddy.
options: Noticing reading patterns in learners' choices
Suggesting books quickly
Fixing the Reading Buddy when it suggests the wrong book
Making sure the Reading Buddy is safe to use
questions.explanation: Noticing patterns and quickly suggesting books are both 'AI performs' tasks. Fixing mistakes and ensuring safety are 'Humans do' tasks.

questions.topic: Humans vs AI: Who Does What
questions.question: Why is 'making sure the Reading Buddy is safe to use' a human task and not an AI task?
options: Because ensuring safety is a responsibility, and responsibility belongs to humans on duty
Because AI cannot notice anything
Because safety does not matter for AI
Because only computers can judge safety
questions.explanation: Safety is a matter of responsibility, and this chapter teaches that responsibility stays with humans, who remain 'on duty.'

questions.topic: Humans vs AI: Who Does What
questions.question: Why is 'noticing reading patterns in learners' choices' something the AI performs, not a human task?
options: Because quickly finding patterns in lots of data is exactly what AI is good at
Because humans are never allowed to notice patterns
Because patterns are not related to the Reading Buddy
Because only companies can notice patterns
questions.explanation: AI is especially good at quickly finding patterns in large amounts of data, which is why this is listed as an 'AI performs' task.

questions.topic: Humans vs AI: Who Does What
questions.question: A student sorts 'choosing which rules the Reading Buddy must follow' into 'AI performs.' What is wrong with this?
options: Setting the rules an AI must follow is a human responsibility, not something AI decides for itself
This sorting is correct
Rules do not matter for AI
AI always chooses its own rules
questions.explanation: Humans must decide the rules an AI follows — this is a 'Humans do' task, not something the AI performs on its own.

questions.topic: Humans vs AI: Who Does What
questions.question: 'Suggesting books quickly' belongs in the 'AI performs' column because giving fast suggestions is a task the AI itself carries out.
questions.explanation: Giving fast suggestions is exactly the kind of everyday task the AI performs by itself.

questions.topic: Humans vs AI: Who Does What
questions.question: Since the AI Reading Buddy suggests books, it should also be the one responsible for fixing itself when it makes a mistake.
questions.explanation: The chapter teaches that fixing mistakes is a human task — humans stay 'on duty' to correct AI errors, even though the AI performs the everyday suggesting.

questions.topic: Humans vs AI: Who Does What
questions.question: Which of these best separates 'Humans do' tasks from 'AI performs' tasks in this chapter?
options: Humans handle responsibility, rules, and safety; AI handles fast, repeated actions like noticing patterns or suggesting things
Humans do nothing at all once AI is built
AI is responsible for setting its own rules
There is no difference between the two
questions.explanation: This is exactly the pattern shown in the Reading Buddy sorting activity.

questions.topic: Humans vs AI: Who Does What
questions.question: A learner keeps getting the same few books suggested again and again. Whose task is it to notice and fix this problem?
options: Humans, since fixing mistakes is a human responsibility
The AI, since it should fix its own bugs
No one needs to fix this
The books themselves
questions.explanation: Fixing problems with the Reading Buddy is a human responsibility, according to the sorting activity.

questions.topic: Humans vs AI: Who Does What
questions.question: Which task shows the Reading Buddy's own everyday work?
options: Suggesting books quickly
Being accountable for mistakes
Deciding legal responsibility
Writing the safety rules
questions.explanation: Suggesting books quickly is the AI's everyday job — an 'AI performs' task.

questions.topic: Humans vs AI: Who Does What
questions.question: Select ALL statements that correctly match a task to 'Humans do.'
options: Fixing the Reading Buddy = Humans do
Choosing the rules = Humans do
Suggesting books quickly = Humans do
Making sure it is safe to use = Humans do
questions.explanation: Fixing, choosing rules, and ensuring safety are 'Humans do' tasks. Suggesting books quickly is an 'AI performs' task, not a human one.

questions.topic: Humans vs AI: Who Does What
questions.question: If the Reading Buddy gives a 'strange suggestion,' who is expected to notice and correct the underlying problem?
options: The humans responsible for the app
The suggestion itself
No one
The other learners
questions.explanation: Humans, not the AI itself, are expected to notice and correct problems with the app.

questions.topic: Humans vs AI: Who Does What
questions.question: Which best explains why humans, not AI, choose the rules an AI must follow?
options: Because humans must decide what is safe and fair before the AI is allowed to act
Because AI cannot read rules
Because rules are unimportant for AI Reading Buddies
Because AI always disagrees with human rules
questions.explanation: Humans decide what is safe and fair, and the AI then follows those rules — this keeps humans in control of important decisions.

questions.topic: Humans vs AI: Who Does What
questions.question: In this chapter's example, humans are responsible for making sure the Reading Buddy is safe to use.
questions.explanation: 'Making sure the Reading Buddy is safe to use' is a 'Humans do' task.

questions.topic: Humans vs AI: Who Does What
questions.question: Which pair correctly matches a task with WHO does it?
options: Noticing reading patterns → AI performs
Noticing reading patterns → Humans do
Choosing the rules → AI performs
Making sure it's safe → AI performs
questions.explanation: Noticing patterns is an 'AI performs' task, while choosing rules and ensuring safety are 'Humans do' tasks.

questions.topic: Humans vs AI: Who Does What
questions.question: What is one thing the AI Reading Buddy is good at, according to the worksheet?
options: Suggesting books quickly
Explaining legal responsibility
Writing new safety laws
Fixing its own mistakes
questions.explanation: The Reading Buddy is designed to suggest books quickly — this is its everyday, 'AI performs' task.

questions.topic: Humans vs AI: Who Does What
questions.question: What is the main lesson of the Reading Buddy sorting activity?
options: AI can perform quick, repetitive tasks, but humans keep responsibility for fixing, rule-setting, and safety
AI should do everything, including making its own rules
Humans should never use AI Reading Buddies
AI and humans do exactly the same tasks
questions.explanation: The activity teaches that AI handles fast, repetitive work while humans keep responsibility for fixing problems, rules, and safety.

questions.topic: Humans vs AI: Who Does What
questions.question: Select ALL tasks below that require ongoing human responsibility, according to the chapter.
options: Fixing mistakes
Choosing safety rules
Making sure something is safe to use
Giving instant suggestions
questions.explanation: Fixing mistakes, choosing rules, and ensuring safety all need ongoing human responsibility. Giving instant suggestions is an AI task.

questions.topic: Humans vs AI: Who Does What
questions.question: Which of these tasks would most likely be listed under 'AI performs'?
options: Noticing patterns in what learners choose to read
Deciding what counts as a safe suggestion
Taking legal responsibility for a mistake
Writing rules for the Reading Buddy
questions.explanation: Noticing patterns is a data-driven task that the AI performs, unlike responsibility, safety decisions, or rule-writing.

questions.topic: Humans vs AI: Who Does What
questions.question: Someone argues, 'Since the AI notices patterns and gives fast suggestions, it should also decide its own safety rules.' Why does this go against the chapter's teaching?
options: Because the chapter teaches that safety and rule-setting stay a human responsibility, even though AI can notice patterns and give suggestions
Because AI cannot notice patterns at all
Because the chapter says AI should always decide its own rules
Because safety rules are not important
questions.explanation: Even though AI performs pattern-noticing and suggesting, safety and rule-setting must remain human responsibilities, per the chapter.

questions.topic: Who Is Responsible When AI Apps Go Wrong
questions.question: If an AI doctor app gives wrong medical advice, who is responsible?
options: The phone where the app is installed
The company that created and operates the app
The AI system itself
No one is responsible
questions.explanation: The worksheet states the company that created and operates the app is responsible, not the phone or the AI system itself.

questions.topic: Who Is Responsible When AI Apps Go Wrong
questions.question: According to the chapter, the AI system itself is responsible if an AI doctor app gives wrong medical advice.
questions.explanation: The chapter says the company that created and operates the app is responsible, not the AI system itself.

questions.topic: Who Is Responsible When AI Apps Go Wrong
questions.question: Which of these is NOT responsible for an AI doctor app's wrong advice, according to the chapter?
options: The company that created and operates the app
The phone where the app is installed
Company leaders who approved the app
The team that built the app
questions.explanation: The phone is just a device; the company (its leaders and team) that created and operates the app is responsible.

questions.topic: Who Is Responsible When AI Apps Go Wrong
questions.question: Why is the phone NOT responsible for the AI doctor app's mistake?
options: The phone is just a device; it does not create or control what the app says
The phone controls all of the AI's decisions
Phones are always to blame for software errors
The phone is more responsible than the company
questions.explanation: A phone is just a device that runs the app; it has no control over what the AI decides to say.

questions.topic: Who Is Responsible When AI Apps Go Wrong
questions.question: Why is the AI system itself not treated as 'responsible' the way a company is?
options: Because the AI cannot be held legally accountable — it doesn't own choices or pay for mistakes; the company that built and runs it does
Because AI never makes medical mistakes
Because AI is smarter than any company
Because responsibility does not matter for AI doctor apps
questions.explanation: Legal accountability belongs to people and companies, not to the AI software itself.

questions.topic: Who Is Responsible When AI Apps Go Wrong
questions.question: A user says, 'It's the app's fault, not the company's, since the app gave the wrong advice.' What is the flaw in this reasoning?
options: The app doesn't have legal responsibility — the company that made and operates it does
There is no flaw in this reasoning
The app is a person and can be blamed
Companies are never responsible for their apps
questions.explanation: An app cannot be held legally responsible; the company behind it is.

questions.topic: Who Is Responsible When AI Apps Go Wrong
questions.question: Select ALL that are true about responsibility for an AI doctor app's mistakes.
options: The company that made and runs the app is responsible
The phone is responsible
The AI system alone is responsible
People can be harmed if medical AI gives wrong advice
questions.explanation: The company is responsible, and wrong medical advice really can harm people. The phone and the AI system alone are not treated as responsible.

questions.topic: Who Is Responsible When AI Apps Go Wrong
questions.question: Why does responsibility for wrong medical advice matter so much?
options: Because wrong medical advice could seriously harm a person's health
Because medical advice is never important
Because phones need to be protected
Because only doctors can use apps
questions.explanation: Wrong medical advice can seriously harm someone's health, which is why responsibility for it matters so much.

questions.topic: Who Is Responsible When AI Apps Go Wrong
questions.question: A company can avoid all responsibility for its AI doctor app simply by saying 'the AI made the mistake, not us.'
questions.explanation: The chapter teaches that the company that creates and operates an AI app remains responsible for its mistakes, not the AI itself.

questions.topic: Who Is Responsible When AI Apps Go Wrong
questions.question: Which best fits the chapter's teaching about AI apps that give advice (medical, or otherwise)?
options: The humans and companies behind the AI stay responsible for what it tells people
Only the user of the app is responsible
Devices like phones are responsible for app content
No one needs to check AI advice once it is released
questions.explanation: Responsibility for AI's advice stays with the humans and companies behind it, not the device or the user alone.

questions.topic: Who Is Responsible When AI Apps Go Wrong
questions.question: Complete the idea: If an AI app makes a serious mistake, responsibility falls on ____.
options: the company that created and operates it
the phone battery
the internet provider
the app store icon
questions.explanation: Responsibility falls on the company that created and operates the app.

questions.topic: Who Is Responsible When AI Apps Go Wrong
questions.question: How is the AI doctor app example similar to the AI Reading Buddy example?
options: In both, responsibility for mistakes belongs to the humans/company behind the AI, not the AI device itself
In both, the AI itself is legally responsible
In both, phones are responsible
In both, no one is responsible
questions.explanation: Both examples show that responsibility stays with the humans/company behind the AI.

questions.topic: Who Is Responsible When AI Apps Go Wrong
questions.question: Select ALL reasons a company (not the AI) is responsible when an AI doctor app gives wrong advice.
options: The company built and operates the app
The company can be held legally accountable
The AI cannot answer for its own mistakes
The phone decided what advice to give
questions.explanation: The company built and operates the app and can be held legally accountable, while the AI itself cannot answer for its mistakes. The phone has no role in deciding advice.

questions.topic: Who Is Responsible When AI Apps Go Wrong
questions.question: Which of these groups created and operates an AI doctor app, and so holds responsibility for it?
options: The company
The phone
The Wi-Fi router
The app's mascot picture
questions.explanation: The company that created and operates the app holds responsibility for it.

questions.topic: Who Is Responsible When AI Apps Go Wrong
questions.question: Why might it be tempting — but wrong — to blame 'the AI system itself' for medical mistakes?
options: Because it can feel like the mistake came from the AI, but real responsibility belongs to the humans/company that built and run it
Because AI systems always intend to cause harm
Because blaming the AI is always correct
Because AI systems can be taken to court
questions.explanation: It may feel like the AI caused the mistake, but true responsibility rests with the humans and company behind it.

questions.topic: Who Is Responsible When AI Apps Go Wrong
questions.question: According to the chapter, phones are responsible for the mistakes made by apps installed on them.
questions.explanation: Phones are just devices — the company that created and operates the app is responsible, not the phone.

questions.topic: Who Is Responsible When AI Apps Go Wrong
questions.question: What lesson from the AI doctor app example connects to the chapter's title, 'Humans on Duty'?
options: Humans (through the company) must stay responsible even when an AI app is doing the day-to-day work
Once an AI app is released, humans have no more duties
Phones are 'on duty' instead of humans
AI apps are always correct so no duty is needed
questions.explanation: Even though the AI does the day-to-day work, humans through the company must stay on duty and responsible.

questions.topic: Who Is Responsible When AI Apps Go Wrong
questions.question: According to the worksheet, which option correctly completes: 'If an AI doctor app gives wrong medical advice, who is responsible?'
options: The company that created and operates the app
The AI system itself
The phone where the app is installed
The internet connection
questions.explanation: The worksheet's correct answer is the company that created and operates the app.

questions.topic: What the Law Requires of AI Companies
questions.question: According to laws mentioned in the chapter, what must AI companies do?
options: Only make AI that never makes mistakes
Test AI for safety and fix problems when they occur
Let AI learn everything on its own
Keep all AI mistakes secret
questions.explanation: The worksheet states that, by law, AI companies must test AI for safety and fix problems when they occur.

questions.topic: What the Law Requires of AI Companies
questions.question: The law says AI companies must make AI that never makes any mistakes.
questions.explanation: The chapter says the law requires companies to test for safety and fix problems, not to guarantee an AI that never errs.

questions.topic: What the Law Requires of AI Companies
questions.question: Why would 'only make AI that never makes mistakes' be an unrealistic legal requirement?
options: No AI system can be guaranteed to be perfect, so the law instead requires testing and fixing problems
All AI systems are already perfect
Mistakes are not possible in computer programs
Laws never mention mistakes
questions.explanation: Since no AI can be guaranteed perfect, the law requires ongoing testing and fixing instead.

questions.topic: What the Law Requires of AI Companies
questions.question: Why doesn't the law allow AI to 'learn everything on its own' without human oversight?
options: Because letting AI learn without any human checks could lead to unsafe or unfair outcomes
Because AI is not capable of learning at all
Because learning is illegal for computers
Because only humans are allowed to learn
questions.explanation: Letting AI learn with no human checks could lead to unsafe or unfair results, which is why oversight is required.

questions.topic: What the Law Requires of AI Companies
questions.question: Select ALL legal duties of AI companies described in the chapter.
options: Test AI for safety
Fix problems when they occur
Let AI learn everything on its own with no oversight
Guarantee AI never makes any mistake
questions.explanation: The two legal duties described are testing for safety and fixing problems when they occur.

questions.topic: What the Law Requires of AI Companies
questions.question: A company claims, 'Our AI is perfect and will never make a mistake, so we don't need to keep testing it.' What is wrong with this claim?
options: The law requires ongoing testing and fixing, because no AI can be guaranteed perfect
This claim is correct and testing is unnecessary
Testing AI is against the law
Only new AI systems need testing
questions.explanation: No AI can be guaranteed perfect, so the law requires ongoing testing and fixing rather than a one-time guarantee.

questions.topic: What the Law Requires of AI Companies
questions.question: What TWO things does the law require of AI companies, according to the chapter?
options: Testing for safety and fixing problems
Making AI faster and prettier
Letting AI learn on its own
Hiding mistakes from users
questions.explanation: The law requires testing AI for safety and fixing problems when they occur.

questions.topic: What the Law Requires of AI Companies
questions.question: According to the chapter, once an AI company tests its product one time, it has fulfilled all of its legal duties forever.
questions.explanation: The homework helper example shows that a company must keep checking daily even after fixing a problem — safety testing is ongoing, not a one-time task.

questions.topic: What the Law Requires of AI Companies
questions.question: Which best explains why 'test AI for safety and fix problems when they occur' is the legally correct duty (not 'never make mistakes')?
options: It is realistic: it accepts that problems can happen but requires companies to catch and correct them
It means companies never have to check their AI
It means mistakes are always someone else's fault
It means AI should be left to learn on its own
questions.explanation: This duty is realistic — it accepts mistakes can happen but requires companies to catch and fix them.

questions.topic: What the Law Requires of AI Companies
questions.question: Which option is closest to what real-world laws (like those enforced by the FTC in this chapter) expect from AI companies?
options: Responsible testing and fixing of problems
Making bold claims with no proof
Ignoring user complaints
Letting AI operate with zero human checks
questions.explanation: Real-world laws, as shown by the FTC case in this chapter, expect responsible testing and fixing of problems.

questions.topic: What the Law Requires of AI Companies
questions.question: Select ALL statements that are FALSE about legal duties of AI companies (per the chapter).
options: Companies must guarantee AI that never makes mistakes
Companies can let AI learn everything with no oversight
Companies must test AI for safety
Companies must fix problems when they occur
questions.explanation: Guaranteeing perfection and letting AI learn with no oversight are both FALSE — the real duties are testing for safety and fixing problems.

questions.topic: What the Law Requires of AI Companies
questions.question: If an AI company discovers its app has a safety problem, what does the law expect the company to do?
options: Fix the problem
Ignore it and hope no one notices
Blame the AI and do nothing
Shut down the whole internet
questions.explanation: The law expects the company to fix safety problems it discovers.

questions.topic: What the Law Requires of AI Companies
questions.question: How does the homework helper's 5-step response show the company meeting its legal duty to 'fix problems when they occur'?
options: The company stops the harmful feature, investigates, fixes the code, tests it, and keeps monitoring
The company does nothing after turning the feature off
The company blames students for the wrong answers
The company waits for the government to fix it
questions.explanation: The full 5-step sequence — stop, investigate, fix, test, and monitor — is exactly how a company fixes problems when they occur.

questions.topic: What the Law Requires of AI Companies
questions.question: What does 'test AI for safety' most likely mean in practice?
options: Checking the AI works correctly and safely before and after release
Only checking the AI once, before it is ever built
Never checking the AI at all
